questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my French. I also love France and wanted to explore Paris.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had many introduction meetings for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I lived in a shared flat with other exchange students from Denmark. I found it on Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will regret it if you live in Cergy. Cergy is kind of a ghetto, and despite the travel from Paris to Cergy, it is much more worth it living in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Ms. Gomert deals with everything regarding to exchange students. In the first weeks you were allowed to try several courses and after you had to inform Ms. Gomert of which courses you actually wanted to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were responding quite fast on e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some LLM classes were only for british or american students, which I found a bit sad, since I wanted to attend some of those classes. Some were despite from the syllabus, not available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get as many courses as possible pre-approved, because it is not certain that you'll be able to attend the ones you actually want to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very old school, and the exams are in paper. The teachers seem very unmotivated, and the French students don't respect the teacher and keep on talking during the lectures. The students are not that involved in class, and the exams are more learn by heart rather than actually using the law.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They don't teach you how to apply the law, but only what the law is. In many cases you could just read the law yourself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different from UCPH. At UCPH the students are much more involved during classes and lectures. The level at UCPH are much higher than at Cergy-Paris Université. You didn't have any books so the things you could be examined in, was what the professor said at a lecture or during class. The credits don't match the work burden. The most demanding courses are only 3 etcs, while courses where you are almost not involved are 6 ects.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to british law
Torts
Tort law (LLM)
Corporate law
Intellectual property
Business law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Corporate law, intellectual property and tort law (LLM). The professors are more motivated in these courses and don't just read the law for you.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - people are very friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. The French students are not that good in English, and they prefer being with their own friend group.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were good at helping you with your French if someone only spoke French.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't live in Cergy
2) By a monthly navigo card with all zones
3) Don't live alone

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go to the train station at Cergy Prefecture at night. It is very scary both in daytime and even more in the evening.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To explore Paris

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language
